forecast-period.text: A trough ahead of a strong cold front is expected move over western SA today, and track east across the rest of SA on Friday. A ridge remains over northern SA on Saturday while a series of troughs and cold fronts move across the state early next week.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Showers and thunderstorms developing in the far west during the afternoon, moving east and reaching the Eyre Peninsula in the evening. Thunderstorms may become severe with damaging wind gusts west of about Ceduna. Dry elsewhere. Maximum temperatures average to above average. Northeast to northwesterly winds, freshening about the coast and in the west during the day.

Showers and thunderstorms moving across central and western SA, clearing from the west later during the day. Thunderstorms may become severe with damaging wind gusts and heavy rainfall about central districts. Maximum temperatures near to above average in the east, grading to below average in the west. Northeast to northwesterly winds, ahead of a west to southwesterly change extending across the state throughout the day. Winds freshening about northern and western inland areas, and about the coast with the change.

Showers about the agricultural areas and adjacent districts, mostly clearing by the afternoon. Isolated thunderstorms possible early across the north and northeast. Maximum temperatures below average. Light winds in the north. West to southwesterly winds across the south.

text.p: Isolated showers and thunderstorms developing across the north and west, extending into central and eastern districts during the evening. Maximum temperatures above average. Northeast to northwesterly winds, fresh at times in the north with a south to southwesterly change moving into the far west during the afternoon.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Sunday: 2 to 5 mm in the North East Pastoral district, broadly increasing to 5 to 15 mm elsewhere with isolated totals of 15 to 25mm. Totals of 25 to 35 mm are possible with thunderstorms over the Eyre Peninsula.
